accepted.s:
The later exactions imposed on indigo cultivators in Champaran included:
1. Sharahbeshi, or enhanced rent.
2. Tawan, or lump-sum compensation demanded when indigo lost its value.
3. Abolition of all rent obligations of tenants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Sharahbeshi was enhanced rent, while tawan was lump-sum compensation extracted when indigo became less valuable. The system did not abolish the tenants’ rent obligations.
accepted.tq: Separate the two genuine exactions from the absolute claim about abolition of rent.
accepted.sec: ■ Indigo system in Champaran - Tinkathia  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which event is regarded as the precursor to the Champaran indigo movement?
accepted.x: The Bengal Indigo Revolt of 1859 preceded and served as an important precursor to the later indigo-related mobilisation in Champaran.
accepted.tq: Identify the earlier related movement rather than the later Gandhian campaign.
accepted.sec: ■ Indigo system in Champaran - Tinkathia  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Ahmedabad Mill Strike associated with Mahatma Gandhi took place during:
accepted.x: The Ahmedabad Mill Strike took place in February–March 1918.
accepted.tq: Use the month range to distinguish closely placed movements.
accepted.sec: ■ Chronological order  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Rowlatt Satyagraha was observed on an all-India basis on:
accepted.x: The all-India hartal and Satyagraha against the Rowlatt legislation took place on 6 April 1919.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the date of the satyagraha from the dates of the Act, massacre and withdrawal.
accepted.sec: ■ Chronological order  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Jallianwala Bagh firing is correct?
1. It took place on Baisakhi, 13 April 1919.
2. Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer blocked the exits.
3. Dyer ordered firing without giving the gathering a warning.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The firing occurred on Baisakhi, Dyer blocked the exits and ordered firing without warning.
accepted.tq: Confirm each statement against the event’s date, commander and immediate action.
accepted.sec: ■ Jallianwala Bagh - Dyer, Viceroy, Hunter Committee, renunciations  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: How many rounds were fired by the troops under General Dyer at Jallianwala Bagh?
accepted.x: The troops fired 1,650 rounds at the unarmed gathering.
accepted.tq: Choose the precise numerical figure rather than a nearby casualty-related number.
accepted.sec: ■ Jallianwala Bagh - Dyer, Viceroy, Hunter Committee, renunciations  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: According to the official figures, the casualties in the Jallianwala Bagh firing were approximately:
accepted.x: The official figures recorded 379 deaths and 1,100 injuries, although the Indian National Congress estimated a higher death toll.
accepted.tq: Keep official figures separate from alternative estimates and firing-round data.
accepted.sec: ■ Jallianwala Bagh - Dyer, Viceroy, Hunter Committee, renunciations  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who was the Lieutenant-Governor of Punjab when the Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred?
accepted.x: Michael O'Dwyer was the Lieutenant-Governor of Punjab. Reginald Dyer was the officer who ordered the firing at Jallianwala Bagh.
accepted.tq: Separate the provincial administrator from the officer who conducted the firing.
accepted.sec: ■ Jallianwala Bagh - Dyer, Viceroy, Hunter Committee, renunciations  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Hunter Committee:
1. It was appointed after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
2. It condemned the conduct of General Dyer.
3. The House of Lords supported Dyer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Hunter Committee was appointed after the massacre and condemned Dyer’s conduct, while the House of Lords backed him.
accepted.tq: Test the contrast between the official inquiry’s condemnation and the House of Lords’ support.
accepted.sec: ■ Jallianwala Bagh - Dyer, Viceroy, Hunter Committee, renunciations  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Mahatma Gandhi gave up which distinction in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
o: Order of the Star of India
accepted.x: Gandhi surrendered the Kaiser-i-Hind medal in protest. Rabindranath Tagore renounced his knighthood.
accepted.tq: Match the protester with the specific honour he relinquished.
accepted.sec: ■ Jallianwala Bagh - Dyer, Viceroy, Hunter Committee, renunciations  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Mahatma Gandhi stayed in South Africa from 1893 until his return to India. Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Phoenix Settlement was established in 1904 near Durban. Tolstoy Farm was established in 1910 near Johannesburg.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure pair linking the settlement, year and location.
accepted.sec: ■ Gandhi in South Africa and return  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Tolstoy Farm, associated with Gandhi’s South African phase, was established in 1910 near:
accepted.x: Tolstoy Farm was established in 1910 near Johannesburg.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the locations of Gandhi’s two South African settlements.
accepted.sec: ■ Gandhi in South Africa and return  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following was the journal published by Mahatma Gandhi during his South African period?
accepted.x: Indian Opinion was the journal associated with Gandhi’s South African period. Young India, Harijan and Navajivan were associated with his later Indian activities.
accepted.tq: Use the geographical phase to identify the corresponding publication.
accepted.sec: ■ Gandhi in South Africa and return  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with Gandhi’s intellectual influences?
o: Lord Curzon — political mentor of Gandhi
Henry David Thoreau — influence on Gandhi
accepted.x: Lord Curzon was not Gandhi’s political mentor. Tolstoy, Ruskin’s Unto This Last and Thoreau influenced Gandhi, while Gopal Krishna Gokhale was his political mentor.
accepted.tq: Find the mismatched person among a group of genuine intellectual influences.
accepted.sec: ■ Gandhi in South Africa and return  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Gandhi returned to India on 9 January 1915. This date is commemorated as:
accepted.x: Pravasi Bharatiya Divas commemorates Gandhi’s return to India from South Africa on 9 January 1915.
accepted.tq: Link the exact date with the commemoration rather than with a movement.
accepted.sec: ■ Gandhi in South Africa and return  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: After returning to India, Gandhi spent about a year touring the country without taking political positions on the advice of:
accepted.x: Gopal Krishna Gokhale advised Gandhi to tour India for a year without taking political positions, enabling him to understand the country’s conditions.
accepted.tq: Identify the mentor connected with the specific advice rather than a general nationalist association.
accepted.sec: ■ Gandhi in South Africa and return  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT a journal associated with Mahatma Gandhi?
accepted.x: Mathrubhumi was not associated with Gandhi. Young India, Navajivan and Harijan were among his journals.
accepted.tq: Eliminate the outsider from a closely related list of publications.
accepted.sec: ■ Gandhi's newspapers, writings and ashrams  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: The Story of My Experiments with Truth — 1915
Young India — Gandhi’s South African autobiography
Harijan — a work written by Henry Thoreau
accepted.x: Hind Swaraj was written in 1909. The Story of My Experiments with Truth was Gandhi’s autobiography, while Young India and Harijan were journals.
accepted.tq: Match a writing with its correct year while rejecting swapped genres and authors.
accepted.sec: ■ Gandhi's newspapers, writings and ashrams  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following ashrams in chronological order of their establishment:
A. Sabarmati Ashram
B. Sevagram Ashram
C. Satyagraha Ashram at Kochrab
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Satyagraha Ashram at Kochrab was established in 1915, Sabarmati Ashram in 1917 and Sevagram in Wardha in 1936.
accepted.tq: Place the earliest and latest ashrams first, then resolve the middle date.
accepted.sec: ■ Gandhi's newspapers, writings and ashrams  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Gandhi’s Satyagraha Ashram was established at Kochrab in Ahmedabad in 1915. Sabarmati was in Ahmedabad, Sevagram was in Wardha and Phoenix Settlement was near Durban.
accepted.tq: Use location-based elimination among Gandhi’s Indian and South African settlements.
accepted.sec: ■ Gandhi's newspapers, writings and ashrams  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Sevagram Ashram at Wardha was established in:
accepted.x: Sevagram Ashram at Wardha was established in 1936.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the late ashram date from the two early Ahmedabad ashram dates.
accepted.sec: ■ Gandhi's newspapers, writings and ashrams  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who is credited with giving Gandhi the title ‘Mahatma’?
accepted.x: Rabindranath Tagore is credited with giving Gandhi the title ‘Mahatma’. Subhas Chandra Bose is associated with the title ‘Father of the Nation’ for Gandhi.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the persons associated with Gandhi’s two well-known titles.
accepted.sec: ■ Gandhi's newspapers, writings and ashrams  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Gandhi’s first arrest by the British Government for sedition occurred when he was detained at:
accepted.x: In April 1919 Gandhi was stopped and detained at Palwal while proceeding towards Punjab; the incident contributed to riots.
accepted.tq: Separate the place of the first detention from the place of the later sedition trial.
accepted.sec: ■ First arrest and sedition trial  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Gandhi’s Great Trial:
1. It was held at Ahmedabad in March 1922.
2. The charge was sedition under Section 124A.
3. The charge arose from articles published in Young India.
4. Gandhi was sentenced to six years’ imprisonment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Gandhi’s 1922 Ahmedabad trial concerned sedition under Section 124A in relation to his Young India articles and resulted in a six-year sentence.
accepted.tq: Verify the venue, year, legal provision, publication and sentence together.
accepted.sec: ■ First arrest and sedition trial  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who presided as the judge in Gandhi’s Great Trial at Ahmedabad in 1922?
accepted.x: Judge Broomfield presided over Gandhi’s sedition trial at Ahmedabad in March 1922.
accepted.tq: Match the judicial officer with the trial rather than with the political administration.
accepted.sec: ■ First arrest and sedition trial  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 extended the repressive powers earlier provided under the:
accepted.x: The Rowlatt Act extended the emergency powers of the Defence of India Act, 1915 into the post-war period.
accepted.tq: Identify the earlier statute whose extraordinary powers were continued.
accepted.sec: ■ Rowlatt Act - purpose, provisions, satyagraha, Satyagraha Sabha  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following provisions was associated with the Rowlatt Act?
1. Detention without trial for up to two years.
2. Suspension of habeas corpus.
3. The legal formula ‘No Vakil, No Dalil, No Appeal’.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Act permitted detention without trial for up to two years and suspended habeas corpus, giving rise to the description ‘No Vakil, No Dalil, No Appeal’.
accepted.tq: Recognise the three linked features of the repressive legislation.
accepted.sec: ■ Rowlatt Act - purpose, provisions, satyagraha, Satyagraha Sabha  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following combinations is correctly matched with the Rowlatt Act protests?
o: Jinnah, Malaviya and Mazhar-ul-Haq — resigned in opposition to the Act
Jinnah, Malaviya and Mazhar-ul-Haq — drafted the Hunter Committee report
Jinnah, Malaviya and Mazhar-ul-Haq — served as members of the Satyagraha Sabha
Jinnah, Malaviya and Mazhar-ul-Haq — defended General Dyer
accepted.x: Muhammad Ali Jinnah, Madan Mohan Malaviya and Mazhar-ul-Haq resigned in opposition to the Rowlatt legislation.
accepted.tq: Match the group of political figures with their common act of protest.
accepted.sec: ■ Rowlatt Act - purpose, provisions, satyagraha, Satyagraha Sabha  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Satyagraha Sabha was established in:
accepted.x: The Satyagraha Sabha was formed in Bombay in February 1919, using the networks of the Home Rule League.
accepted.tq: Combine the organisation’s location and date to distinguish it from later events.
accepted.sec: ■ Rowlatt Act - purpose, provisions, satyagraha, Satyagraha Sabha  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Rowlatt Satyagraha hartal of 6 April 1919 was observed through:
o: A campaign for compulsory military recruitment
Armed rebellion and seizure of courts
accepted.x: The 6 April 1919 hartal involved fasting and prayer and became the first all-India mass strike of the movement.
accepted.tq: Identify the method of action from the non-violent character of the satyagraha.
accepted.sec: ■ Rowlatt Act - purpose, provisions, satyagraha, Satyagraha Sabha  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Why did Gandhi call off the Rowlatt Satyagraha on 18 April 1919?
o: The Hunter Committee accepted all nationalist demands
The Rowlatt Act had been repealed
The British Government granted complete independence
accepted.x: Gandhi withdrew the movement on 18 April 1919 after violence occurred, later describing the decision to launch it as a ‘Himalayan blunder’.
accepted.tq: Link the withdrawal to its immediate cause rather than to a political concession.
accepted.sec: ■ Rowlatt Act - purpose, provisions, satyagraha, Satyagraha Sabha  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Gandhi described his decision to launch the Rowlatt Satyagraha as a:
accepted.x: After the movement led to violence and was called off, Gandhi described the decision to launch it as a ‘Himalayan blunder’.
accepted.tq: Recall the distinctive phrase associated with Gandhi’s self-assessment.
accepted.sec: ■ Rowlatt Act - purpose, provisions, satyagraha, Satyagraha Sabha  [other exams, GROUP-II]
